definition: A bond formed between two atoms when the two atoms share a pair of electrons. The shared pair is attracted to the nucleus of both atoms.
msAccepts: a shared pair of electrons between two atoms
bond formed by sharing one or more pairs of electrons

definition: The attraction between opposite charges. In a covalent bond it is the attraction between the shared pair of electrons (negative) and the nuclei (positive) of both bonded atoms.
msAccepts: attraction between the shared electron pair and both nuclei
opposite charges attract

definition: A group of a fixed number of atoms joined together by covalent bonds — from two atoms (diatomic) up to many thousands (proteins, DNA).
msAccepts: a fixed number of atoms joined by covalent bonds
two or more atoms chemically bonded together by sharing electrons

definition: Made of molecules that each contain exactly two atoms — H₂, Cl₂, O₂, N₂, HCl, CO.
msAccepts: molecules containing two atoms
two atoms per molecule

definition: A diagram of covalent bonding showing outer-shell electrons only, with one atom's electrons drawn as dots and the other atom's as crosses to show where each electron came from.
msAccepts: outer shell electrons only
dots and crosses show the origin of each electron
shared pairs drawn between the two atoms

definition: Having the same number of electrons. In covalent bonding, atoms end up isoelectronic with a noble gas: hydrogen with 2 outer electrons, other atoms with 8.
msAccepts: same number of electrons as a noble gas atom
same electron count as helium or another noble gas
msAvoids: the atom has become a noble gas

definition: A pair of electrons in the outer shell of an atom in a molecule that is not involved in covalent bonding. Water's oxygen carries two lone pairs.
msAccepts: pair of outer-shell electrons not used in bonding
electron pair that does not form a covalent bond

definition: A covalent bond made of two shared pairs of electrons — four electrons shared between the two bonded atoms, for example O₂ and CO₂.
msAccepts: two shared pairs of electrons
four shared electrons between two atoms
msAvoids: two separate single bonds side by side
a bond that is twice as long

definition: A covalent bond made of three shared pairs of electrons — six shared electrons between the two bonded atoms, for example N₂.
msAccepts: three shared pairs of electrons
six shared electrons between two atoms
msAvoids: a bond made of three molecules

definition: Shaped like a tetrahedron — a triangular-based pyramid — with one atom at the centre and four atoms at the corners, as in methane. Electron pairs spread as far apart as possible.
msAccepts: four electron pairs arranged as far apart as possible
triangular-based pyramid arrangement, bond angle 109.5°
msAvoids: the atoms are at 90° to each other

definition: Having a slightly positive end and a slightly negative end. Water is polar because the shared electrons are attracted more strongly towards the oxygen atom.
msAccepts: has a δ− and a δ+ end
unequal sharing of the electron pair

definition: The weak forces of attraction between molecules — literally 'between molecules'. They are broken — not the covalent bonds — when a molecular substance melts or boils.
msAccepts: weak forces between molecules
broken when a simple molecular substance melts or boils

definition: A structure made of separate molecules with weak intermolecular forces between them. Substances with this structure are gases, liquids or low-melting solids and usually do not conduct electricity.
msAccepts: molecules with weak forces between them
low melting and boiling points because intermolecular forces are broken
msAvoids: a structure of one giant molecule
molecules held by strong covalent bonds between them

definition: A structure in which atoms are joined by strong covalent bonds continuously in three dimensions — not a molecule, because the number of atoms varies with the size of the crystal. Diamond, graphite and silicon dioxide.
msAccepts: millions of atoms joined by strong covalent bonds
regular 3D network of covalent bonds
high melting point because covalent bonds must be broken

definition: An outer-shell electron that is not fixed in a covalent bond and can move freely through a structure. Graphite's fourth electron per carbon is delocalised within each layer.
msAccepts: electrons free to move through the structure
not tied to any one bond — carry charge through the layer
msAvoids: electrons that have left their shells permanently

definition: One of two or more different forms of the same element in the same physical state. Diamond, graphite and C₆₀ fullerene are all allotropes of carbon.
msAccepts: different structural forms of the same element
same element, different arrangement of atoms
msAvoids: different compounds of the same element
